title: Rongzai agent: A Large Language Model-Based Autonomous Assistant for Rietveld Refinement of Neutron Diffraction Data
summary: Neutron diffraction (ND) is an indispensable technique for determining atomic positions (especially light elements) and thus serves as a critical probe for revealing microscopic structures in materials science. However, traditional Rietveld refinement of ND data relies heavily on manual operation of specialized software, which is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and highly dependent on user expertise, severely hindering automated analysis. The automation of Rietveld refinement has long been a long-standing and challenging problem in crystallography. To address this challenge, this paper presents the Dr.Sai-Rongzai agent, an autonomous refinement assistant based on a large language model (LLM), a specialist knowledge base, and the GSAS-II refinement engine, achieving for the first time an intelligent refinement that integrates knowledge-driven decision-making. The agent accomplishes a fully automated workflow from natural language task parsing to autonomous decision-making, execution of refinement strategies, and report generation. Evaluation on five representative samples shows that the Rongzai agent achieves lower Rwp values than human specialists on three samples (2.88% vs. 4.42%, 5.06% vs. 5.40%, 7.60% vs. 9.00%), while on the other two samples its results are very close to those of the specialists. The agent is currently deployed at the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) and is open for external user registration, providing an intelligent and user-friendly analytical tool for materials research. This work fully leverages the cutting-edge advantages of LLM, offers a new path to solve the long-standing problem of automated refinement, takes a key step toward intelligent and fully automated crystallographic analysis, and holds great potential to accelerate AI for Science discoveries in neutron-based materials characterization.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Dr.Sai-Rongzai, an LLM-based autonomous agent for Rietveld refinement of neutron diffraction data, achieving fully automated workflow from task parsing to report generation with performance comparable or superior to human specialists.
AI.motivation: Traditional Rietveld refinement of neutron diffraction data is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and highly dependent on user expertise, with no existing automated solution—a long-standing challenge in crystallography.
AI.method: The Dr.Sai-Rongzai agent combines a large language model (LLM), a specialist knowledge base, and the GSAS-II refinement engine to enable an intelligent, knowledge-driven, fully automated refinement workflow from natural language task parsing to decision-making, execution, and report generation.
AI.result: On five representative samples, the agent achieved lower Rwp values than human specialists on three samples (2.88% vs. 4.42%, 5.06% vs. 5.40%, 7.60% vs. 9.00%) and comparable results on the other two. The agent is deployed at CSNS and open for external registration.
AI.conclusion: This work leverages LLM advantages to solve the long-standing problem of automated refinement, taking a key step toward intelligent and fully automated crystallographic analysis and accelerating AI for Science discoveries in neutron-based materials characterization.

title: Engineering topological flat bands in $Γ$-valley moiré systems with Ising-type SOC: twisted 1T-ZrS$_2$ and 1T-SnSe$_2$
summary: Twisted moiré superlattices hosting topological flat bands provide a platform to explore the interplay between topology and correlations. Here we investigate topological band structures in $Γ$-valley moiré systems based on 1T-ZrS$_2$ and 1T-SnSe$_2$. Using large-scale ab initio calculations and continuum modelling, we demonstrate that both materials exhibit an approximate spin-$U(1)$ symmetry and host isolated topological moiré valence bands, including quantum spin Hall and high spin Chern states. By constructing a hierarchy of $Γ$-valley moiré continuum models, we show that isolated moiré bands carry a trivial $C_3$ symmetry indicator when the low-energy physics is described by a single effective orbital and a single layer-hybridized branch, either bonding or antibonding. Topological bands therefore arise from inter-branch and/or inter-orbital coupling. Moreover, we determine interaction-driven phase diagrams using Hartree--Fock and exact diagonalization, finding various phases tunable by twist angle, interaction strength, and displacement field. We identify specific conditions under which fractional Chern insulators are favored. Together with previous work showing that the moiré conduction bands of 1T-ZrS$_2$ and 1T-SnSe$_2$ realize $M$-valley twisting and host quasi-one-dimensional physics, our results establish these systems as ideal platforms for strongly correlated moiré physics and provide a systematic framework for understanding topological band structures in $Γ$-valley moiré materials.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates topological band structures in Γ-valley moiré systems (1T-ZrS₂ and 1T-SnSe₂), finding approximate spin-U(1) symmetry, topological moiré valence bands (quantum spin Hall and high spin Chern states), and interaction-driven phases including fractional Chern insulators, establishing these materials as platforms for strongly correlated moiré physics.
AI.motivation: To explore the interplay between topology and correlations in twisted moiré superlattices hosting topological flat bands, specifically focusing on Γ-valley moiré systems based on 1T-ZrS₂ and 1T-SnSe₂.
AI.method: Large-scale ab initio calculations, continuum modelling, hierarchy of Γ-valley moiré continuum models, Hartree-Fock and exact diagonalization methods.
AI.result: Both materials exhibit approximate spin-U(1) symmetry and host isolated topological moiré valence bands (quantum spin Hall and high spin Chern states). Topological bands arise from inter-branch and/or inter-orbital coupling. Interaction-driven phase diagrams show various phases tunable by twist angle, interaction strength, and displacement field, with specific conditions favoring fractional Chern insulators.
AI.conclusion: These Γ-valley moiré systems are ideal platforms for strongly correlated moiré physics, complementing previous work on M-valley twisting and quasi-one-dimensional physics in the conduction bands.

title: Circularity in Perovskite-Based Tandem Photovoltaics for Terawatt-Scale Deployment
summary: As photovoltaics (PVs) scale from one to multiple terawatts over the next decade, ensuring sustainable deployment is urgently required. Crystalline silicon (c-Si) PVs, the current industry standard, will generate an estimated 160 million tonnes of waste by 2050, and there remains complex technoeconomic challenges associated with their recycling. Metal-halide perovskite (MHP)-based tandem PVs not only promise higher power conversion efficiencies than single-junction c-Si devices, but also offer intrinsic advantages for circularity, including simpler device architectures, low-temperature processing, and more accessible materials recovery routes. At this pivotal juncture when perovskite PVs begin to enter the market, this review examines the critical circularity challenges that must be addressed: substitution of scarce raw materials, scalable recycling protocols, cost-effective stack delamination, safe lead sequestration, and policy frameworks to encourage circularity across the device lifecycle with effective incentives. By integrating the materials, technoeconomic and policy dimensions that go beyond conventional lifecycle assessments, we outline actionable strategies to co-optimize device performance and sustainability. This review aims to guide researchers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders in steering perovskite-based tandem PVs towards a circular and responsible commercialization pathway within the global clean-energy transition.

AI.tldr: This review examines circularity challenges for perovskite-based tandem photovoltaics as they enter the market, including material substitution, recycling protocols, delamination, lead sequestration, and policy frameworks, and outlines strategies to co-optimize performance with sustainability for responsible commercialization.
AI.motivation: Crystalline silicon PVs will generate an estimated 160 million tonnes of waste by 2050 with complex recycling challenges, while perovskite tandem PVs offer higher efficiencies and intrinsic circularity advantages, motivating the need to address sustainability issues before market scale-up.
AI.method: This is a review that integrates materials science, technoeconomic analysis, and policy dimensions beyond conventional lifecycle assessments to examine critical circularity challenges for perovskite-based tandem PVs.
AI.result: The review identifies five key circularity challenges: substitution of scarce raw materials, scalable recycling protocols, cost-effective stack delamination, safe lead sequestration, and policy frameworks with effective incentives.
AI.conclusion: Perovskite-based tandem PVs can potentially achieve circular and responsible commercialization if actionable strategies co-optimizing device performance and sustainability are implemented, guided by the integrated materials-technoeconomic-policy framework presented.

title: A Neural-Network Framework to Learn History-Dependent Constitutive Laws and Identifiability of Internal Variables
summary: The identification of constitutive laws is ubiquitous in engineering: in modeling of materials where experimental data are fitted to mathematical models or learning surrogate models to beat the FE\textsuperscript{2} computational cost of multiscale numerical simulations. However, these models of constitutive laws, unless equipped with a potential formulation, are not necessarily consistent with (a) the second law of thermodynamics; (b) stability of the material under extreme applied strain; and (c) the mathematical theory underpinning the existence of solutions of the governing equation. In this work, we present a causal and energetic formulation, consistent with aforementioned properties, of learning a history-dependent constitutive law. This characterization of the class of internal variables sheds light on the equivalence class of equivalent surrogate models for the constitutive law. We show that the internal variables that are learned from the data are unique up to a linear transform. The framework is deployed to learn the Taylor-averaged response of a polycrystalline magnesium unit cell. We achieve 2\% relative error in the prediction of the Taylor-averaged response.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a causal and energetic framework for learning history-dependent constitutive laws that ensures thermodynamic consistency, material stability, and mathematical well-posedness. Internal variables are shown to be unique up to a linear transform, and the method achieves 2% relative error in predicting the Taylor-averaged response of polycrystalline magnesium.
AI.motivation: Constitutive law models, unless equipped with a potential formulation, often violate thermodynamic consistency, material stability under extreme strain, and the mathematical theory ensuring existence of solutions. This work addresses the lack of physically principled constraints in data-driven constitutive modeling.
AI.method: A causal and energetic formulation for learning history-dependent constitutive laws is presented. The framework characterizes the class of internal variables, establishing that learned internal variables are unique up to a linear transform, and is deployed to learn the Taylor-averaged response of a polycrystalline magnesium unit cell.
AI.result: The method achieves 2% relative error in predicting the Taylor-averaged response of polycrystalline magnesium.
AI.conclusion: The proposed causal and energetic framework ensures thermodynamic consistency, material stability, and mathematical well-posedness in learned constitutive laws, with internal variable uniqueness up to a linear transform, demonstrated by accurate prediction of polycrystalline magnesium response.

title: Carrier-density dependence of magnetotransport in correlated Dirac semimetal CaIrO$_3$
summary: We report the carrier density dependence of the magnetotransport property in the correlated Dirac semimetal CaIrO$_3$. In the dilute carrier density region ($n_{\rm H}$ $\sim 2.2 \times 10^{16} \,$$\rm{cm}^{-3}$) at $2 \, \mathrm{K}$, the mobility exceeds $1.0 \times 10^{5} \,$$\rm{cm}^{2}/\rm{Vs}$ at $2 \, \mathrm{K}$, and the transverse magnetoresistance (MR) reaches $2,000 \,$\% at $12 \, \mathrm{T}$. The analysis of quantum oscillations and Hall conductivity shows that the Fermi velocity is nearly independent of the cross-sectional area of the Fermi surface, or equivalently the carrier density, supporting a $k$-linear dispersion of the Dirac node. The field dependence of magnetoresistivity is nearly $B$-linear in the moderate carrier density region ($n_\mathrm{H} \geq 4 \times 10^{16}\,$cm$^{-3}$), but scales with $B^α$ ($α> 2$) in the lower carrier density region. The variation of magnetoresistivity is likely affected by the enhanced long-range Coulomb interaction in the quantum limit, where Dirac electrons are subject to the magnetic confinement.

AI.tldr: Study of CaIrO₃ Dirac semimetal reveals ultrahigh mobility (>10⁵ cm²/Vs) and giant magnetoresistance (2000% at 12 T) at low carrier densities, with Fermi velocity independent of carrier density supporting linear Dirac dispersion, and field-dependent magnetoresistivity transitions from B-linear to B^α (α>2) behavior due to enhanced Coulomb interactions in the quantum limit.
AI.motivation: To investigate how carrier density affects magnetotransport in the correlated Dirac semimetal CaIrO₃, particularly exploring the role of long-range Coulomb interactions in the quantum limit regime.
AI.method: Measured carrier-density-dependent magnetotransport (Hall effect, magnetoresistance, quantum oscillations) in CaIrO₃ thin films at 2 K, analyzing Fermi velocity from quantum oscillations and Hall conductivity, and examining magnetoresistivity scaling exponents.
AI.result: Mobility exceeds 10⁵ cm²/Vs, transverse MR reaches 2000% at 12 T for dilute carrier density (~2.2×10¹⁶ cm⁻³); Fermi velocity is nearly constant with carrier density, confirming k-linear Dirac dispersion; magnetoresistivity is B-linear for moderate densities but follows B^α (α>2) at lower densities.
AI.conclusion: The observed variation in magnetoresistivity scaling likely originates from enhanced long-range Coulomb interactions in the quantum limit where Dirac electrons are magnetically confined.

title: Machine-learning-identified two-dimensional van der Waals multiferroics for four-state nonvolatile memory
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) multiferroics offer an attractive platform for four-state nonvolatile memory by combining switchable ferroelectric polarization and magnetization within a single material system. However, their development is hindered by the scarcity of synthesizable candidates and the lack of non-destructive readout schemes. Here, we combine machine-learning screening with first-principles calculations to explore the 2D vdW ABC$_2$X$_6$ family and identify a set of high-confidence multiferroic candidates. Among them, AuCrP$_2$S$_6$ monolayer emerges as a representative system with a ferromagnetic ground state, a sizable out-of-plane polarization of 7.46 pC/m, and a moderate ferroelectric switching barrier of $\sim$130 meV/f.u. Moreover, the nonlinear optical response mediated by the bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in AuCrP$_2$S$_6$ provides a dual-channel probe of the ferroic orders, in which the polarization direction governs the photocurrent sign while the magnetic order selects the spin channel via robust exchange splitting. This intrinsic coupling enables the non-destructive readout of four logic states within a single atomic layer, thereby providing a practical blueprint for next-generation multistate optoelectronic memory.

AI.tldr: The paper uses machine learning and first-principles calculations to identify 2D vdW multiferroic candidates in the ABC₂X₆ family, with AuCrP₂S₆ monolayer exhibiting ferromagnetism, out-of-plane polarization, and BPVE-mediated non-destructive four-state readout.
AI.motivation: To address the scarcity of synthesizable 2D vdW multiferroic candidates and lack of non-destructive readout schemes for four-state nonvolatile memory applications.
AI.method: Machine-learning screening combined with first-principles calculations to explore the 2D vdW ABC₂X₆ family.
AI.result: AuCrP₂S₆ monolayer is identified as a multiferroic candidate with ferromagnetic ground state, out-of-plane polarization of 7.46 pC/m, and ferroelectric switching barrier of ~130 meV/f.u. Its BPVE enables dual-channel (polarization and magnetic order) non-destructive readout of four logic states.
AI.conclusion: The intrinsic coupling between ferroic orders and BPVE in AuCrP₂S₆ provides a practical blueprint for next-generation multistate optoelectronic memory.

title: Unified definition of ferroelectricity
summary: Recent theoretical and experimental advances in quantum ferroelectrics suggest that ferroelectricity can also emerge in non-polar space group, highlighting the limitations of conventional polar space group criteria in identifying ferroelectric materials. Here, we introduce a unified definition based on switchable polarization differences between energetically equivalent states, which naturally encompasses conventional and quantum ferroelectrics. Guided by this principle, we implement a high-throughput screening strategy that systematically identifies both conventional and quantum ferroelectrics among experimentally synthesized materials. In particular, we identify a new type of quantum ferroelectric in which the quantized polarization arises from arbitrary ionic displacements, in contrast to previous quantum ferroelectrics (including both fractional and integer quantum ferroelectrics) where quantized polarization results from fractional or integer ionic displacements. Notably, we find that materials such as Ba3I6 and Cs2PdC2 exhibit low switching barriers and robust insulating behavior, highlighting their experimental viability. Our results reconcile conventional and quantum ferroelectrics, expand the accessible materials landscape, and provide a practical roadmap for discovering next-generation ferroelectrics with advanced switchable functionalities.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a unified definition of ferroelectricity based on switchable polarization differences between energetically equivalent states, enabling high-throughput screening that identifies both conventional and quantum ferroelectrics, including a new type where quantized polarization arises from arbitrary ionic displacements.
AI.motivation: Recent findings show ferroelectricity can emerge in non-polar space groups, revealing limitations of conventional polar space group criteria. A unified framework is needed to reconcile conventional and quantum ferroelectrics and enable systematic discovery.
AI.method: A unified definition based on switchable polarization differences between energetically equivalent states is proposed. A high-throughput screening strategy is implemented to systematically identify conventional and quantum ferroelectrics from experimentally synthesized materials.
AI.result: Identified a new type of quantum ferroelectric where quantized polarization arises from arbitrary ionic displacements. Materials such as Ba3I6 and Cs2PdC2 show low switching barriers and robust insulating behavior, indicating experimental viability.
AI.conclusion: The work reconciles conventional and quantum ferroelectrics, expands the accessible materials landscape, and provides a practical roadmap for discovering next-generation ferroelectrics with advanced switchable functionalities.

title: Depletion-mode N-polar AlN-based high electron mobility transistors with improved on/off ratios
summary: We report N-polar AlN-based high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with a GaN channel thickness of 5.2 nm on N-polar AlN on sapphire. The threshold voltage is around -2.4 to -3.0 V with saturation currents over 240 mA/mm and on/off ratios as high as 10,000, much higher than previously reported N-polar AlN-based HEMTs. The high on/off ratio is attributed to the use of an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with a dedicated AlN transition layer, together with improved gate leakage. The high frequency properties as well as the on-resistance of ~20 Ohm mm are all limited by the 2000 Ohm/square sheet resistance of the channel layer.

AI.tldr: N-polar AlN-based HEMTs with 5.2 nm GaN channel on sapphire achieve threshold voltage -2.4 to -3.0 V, saturation currents >240 mA/mm, and on/off ratios up to 10,000, attributed to abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with AlN transition layer and improved gate leakage, though performance is limited by 2000 Ohm/square sheet resistance.
AI.motivation: To improve the performance of N-polar AlN-based HEMTs, which previously suffered from low on/off ratios, by engineering the heterostructure and reducing gate leakage.
AI.method: Fabrication of N-polar AlN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire using an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with a dedicated AlN transition layer to enhance interface quality and reduce leakage.
AI.result: Saturation currents >240 mA/mm, on/off ratios up to 10,000, threshold voltage -2.4 to -3.0 V, on-resistance ~20 Ohm mm, but performance limited by 2000 Ohm/square sheet resistance.
AI.conclusion: The improved on/off ratio demonstrates the effectiveness of the optimized heterostructure design, but high sheet resistance remains a bottleneck for high-frequency and low-resistance performance.

title: Ward identities and orbital magnetization in current density functional theory
summary: We revisit the derivation of the orbital magnetization formula for periodic crystals in current density functional theory (CDFT)[1]. Our new derivation computes the linear response of the energy density to a periodic magnetic field in the long-wavelength limit. We unveil a Ward identity which connects the current vertex to the derivative of the Kohn-Sham self-energy. The result of Ref.[1] is confirmed: the orbital magnetization of the interacting solid can be computed exactly (in principle) from the self-consistent eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the Kohn-Sham equation of CDFT.

AI.tldr: The paper rederives the orbital magnetization formula for periodic crystals in current density functional theory (CDFT), confirming that orbital magnetization can be computed exactly from Kohn-Sham eigenfunctions and eigenvalues. A Ward identity connecting the current vertex to the derivative of the Kohn-Sham self-energy is unveiled.
AI.motivation: To revisit and provide a new derivation of the orbital magnetization formula for periodic crystals within CDFT, and to confirm the validity of the existing result in Ref.[1].
AI.method: The derivation computes the linear response of the energy density to a periodic magnetic field in the long-wavelength limit, and unveils a Ward identity that connects the current vertex to the derivative of the Kohn-Sham self-energy.
AI.result: The result of Ref.[1] is confirmed: the orbital magnetization of the interacting solid can be computed exactly (in principle) from the self-consistent eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the Kohn-Sham equation of CDFT.
AI.conclusion: The derived Ward identity and the new derivation provide a more rigorous foundation for the orbital magnetization formula in interacting periodic crystals within CDFT.

title: Chiroptical Ternary Entropy Harvesting from Self-Assembled Block Copolymer Nanopatterns
summary: Nanoscale fabrication inevitably produces local stochasticity that is commonly treated as a defect, but can instead be harnessed as a material resource for information security. Here we report a chiroptical platform for ternary entropy harvesting based on stochastic Au nanopatterns formed by block copolymer self-assembly. By transducing fabrication-induced stochastic microstates into handedness-dependent optical responses through chiroptical mapping, our platform enables native ternary digitization rather than conventional binary encoding, allowing physically harvested ternary random sequences to be used for key generation. This raises the information density to log2(3) = 1.585 bits per trit, approximately 58.5% higher than the binary limit, enabling more entropy to be harvested from a limited physical footprint. The harvested outputs exhibit near-balanced symbol populations, negligible spatial and inter-sample correlations, Shannon entropy approaching the ternary ideal, and resistance to statistical and machine-learning-based prediction. These results establish self-assembled chiroptical nanostructures as a scalable platform for cryptographic key generation, secure edge devices, and distributed Internet-of-Things platforms.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a chiroptical platform that harnesses stochasticity from nanoscale fabrication (block copolymer self-assembled Au nanopatterns) for ternary entropy harvesting, enabling physically generated random sequences with 1.585 bits per trit (58.5% higher density than binary) for cryptographic key generation.
AI.motivation: To transform nanoscale fabrication-induced stochasticity from a defect into a resource for information security, moving beyond conventional binary encoding to achieve higher entropy density in physically harvested random sequences.
AI.method: Stochastic Au nanopatterns formed by block copolymer self-assembly are used as a chiroptical platform. Fabrication-induced stochastic microstates are transduced into handedness-dependent optical responses via chiroptical mapping, enabling native ternary digitization rather than binary encoding.
AI.result: The platform achieves 1.585 bits per trit (58.5% higher than binary limit), near-balanced symbol populations, negligible spatial and inter-sample correlations, Shannon entropy approaching the ternary ideal, and resistance to statistical and ML-based prediction attacks.
AI.conclusion: Self-assembled chiroptical nanostructures provide a scalable platform for cryptographic key generation, secure edge devices, and distributed IoT applications by physically harvesting ternary entropy from nanoscale stochasticity.

title: From spin splitting to projected mass in altermagnetic Chern matter
summary: Altermagnetic spin splitting alone does not define Chern matter. The relevant object is the exchange mass projected onto Hall-active surface, valley, orbital or interface sectors. We formulate this projected-mass criterion for compensated magnetic topology. The resulting two-channel $(C,\mathcal{A})$ diagnostic separates hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases in a global insulating gap. It also guides interface, thickness and materials design strategies.

AI.tldr: Altermagnetic spin splitting alone does not define Chern matter; instead, the exchange mass projected onto Hall-active sectors determines compensated magnetic topology. A two-channel (C, 𝒜) diagnostic separates hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases.
AI.motivation: To clarify that altermagnetic spin splitting is insufficient for defining topological Chern matter, and to establish a projected-mass criterion for identifying hidden Hall responses in compensated magnetic systems.
AI.method: Formulates a projected-mass criterion for compensated magnetic topology, introducing a two-channel (C, 𝒜) diagnostic that distinguishes hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases.
AI.result: The projected-mass criterion enables separation of hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases within a global insulating gap.
AI.conclusion: The criterion guides interface, thickness, and materials design strategies for engineering topological phases in compensated magnets.

title: Strain-Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution, Electrical, Optical, and Thermoelectric Properties of the Multifunctional 2D CrSi2N4 Monolayer
summary: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) is employed to evaluate the structural, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and electrocatalytic properties of monolayer CrSi2N4. Its symmetric N-Si-N-Cr-N-Si-N septuple-layer structure exhibits dynamic, thermal (300 K), and mechanical stability, supported by a -8.76 eV/atom cohesive energy. PBE and HSE06 functionals reveal an indirect bandgap of 0.58 eV and 2.16 eV, respectively, driven by localized Cr-3d and N-2p states. The monolayer features 15.57 static dielectric constant and maximum absorption coefficients of 0.9 X 10^6 cm-1 (visible) and 1.4 X 10^6 cm-1 (deep-UV). Semiclassical Boltzmann calculations predict an outstanding room-temperature n-type thermoelectric power factor of 3.5 x mW/mK2. For hydrogen evolution (HER), the basal plane yields a baseline hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH) of 1.05 eV at the N-site. Applying +5% expansive biaxial strain improves HER kinetics, reducing ΔGH to 0.46 eV. Thus, CrSi2N4 is a resilient, tuneable candidate for waste-heat recovery, photodetectors, and sustainable electrocatalysis.

AI.tldr: First-principles DFT study evaluates monolayer CrSi2N4, finding it dynamically/thermally/mechanically stable with bandgaps of 0.58 eV (PBE) and 2.16 eV (HSE06), strong visible and deep-UV absorption, high n-type thermoelectric power factor (3.5 mW/mK²), and HER catalytic activity improvable via +5% biaxial strain (ΔGH reduced from 1.05 eV to 0.46 eV).
AI.motivation: To assess the structural, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and electrocatalytic properties of monolayer CrSi2N4 as a potential multifunctional 2D material for energy conversion and optoelectronics.
AI.method: First-principles DFT with PBE and HSE06 functionals; semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory for thermoelectric properties; hydrogen adsorption free energy calculations for HER activity under biaxial strain.
AI.result: Monolayer CrSi2N4 is stable with bandgaps of 0.58 eV (PBE) and 2.16 eV (HSE06); static dielectric constant of 15.57; peak absorption 0.9×10⁶ cm⁻¹ (visible) and 1.4×10⁶ cm⁻¹ (deep-UV). Thermoelectric power factor of 3.5 mW/mK² at 300 K for n-type. Basal plane HER ΔGH = 1.05 eV; with +5% biaxial strain, ΔGH improves to 0.46 eV.
AI.conclusion: CrSi2N4 is a stable, tunable 2D material promising for waste-heat recovery, photodetectors, and sustainable electrocatalysis.

title: Shaping Maximally Localized Wannier Functions via Discrete Adiabatic Transport
summary: Maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs) are conventionally constructed by iteratively minimizing a spread functional over a high-dimensional gauge landscape. In this work, we present a non-variational constructive algorithm that unifies gauge smoothing and the eigenvalue problem of the projected position operator into a single deterministic framework. We demonstrate that discrete adiabatic transport across band degeneracies emerges naturally as an integral part of the solution procedure for the position eigenvectors. In this transport-aligned gauge, the Bloch overlaps exhibit an approximately linear phase dependence, allowing the Wannier centers to be extracted via deterministic fixed-point iterations and self-consistent updates rather than spread-functional minimization. Benchmark calculations for one- and two-dimensional systems yield spreads and orbital shapes in good agreement with standard minimization schemes. Furthermore, this analytical approach transparently isolates the physical origin of the $\mathcal{O}(L)$ mesh-dependent spread scaling ($L$ being the boundary seam resolution) observed in graphene, demonstrating that it is an intrinsic geometric manifestation of non-commuting projected position operators forcing finite gauge defects to accumulate along a one-dimensional boundary seam.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a non-variational constructive algorithm for generating maximally localized Wannier functions, replacing iterative spread functional minimization with a deterministic framework based on discrete adiabatic transport and fixed-point iterations.
AI.motivation: Conventional MLWF construction relies on iterative minimization of a spread functional over a high-dimensional gauge landscape, which is computationally expensive and lacks direct physical interpretability.
AI.method: The method unifies gauge smoothing and the eigenvalue problem of the projected position operator into a single deterministic framework. It leverages discrete adiabatic transport across band degeneracies to construct a transport-aligned gauge, where Bloch overlaps exhibit approximately linear phase dependence, enabling Wannier center extraction via fixed-point iterations and self-consistent updates.
AI.result: Benchmark calculations for 1D and 2D systems yield spreads and orbital shapes consistent with standard minimization schemes. The method analytically identifies that the 𝒪(L) mesh-dependent spread scaling in graphene originates from non-commuting projected position operators forcing gauge defects to accumulate along a one-dimensional boundary seam.
AI.conclusion: The non-variational approach provides a physically transparent and computationally efficient alternative to conventional MLWF construction, and offers new insights into the geometric origin of mesh-dependent spread scaling in 2D materials.

title: Accurate computation of the electron-phonon interaction contribution to the total energy
summary: The standard Hamiltonian of a coupled electron-phonon system is based on second-order perturbation theory. The EPI contribution in the standard Hamiltonian consists of two terms, the EPI contribution to the band-structure energy and the partial-Fan-Migdal (FM)-occupied contribution. Within the non-adiabatic approximation, we derive a new expression for the partial-FM-occ contribution and show that it has the structure of a higher-order term, and not a second-order term. Along similar lines, we derive new expressions for the computation of the partial-FM-occ term. The new expressions for the partial-FM-occ term must be preferred over the standard expressions, in theoretical and computational studies, because they incorporate the complete physics underlying this term. Unlike the EPI contribution to individual eigenstates, the EPI contribution to the total energy must be computed in the non-adiabatic approximation for all materials, Infra-red (IR) active and IR-inactive. We report the computation of the standard Hamiltonian, for the first time, for Carbon polymorphs (diamond and hexagonal lonsdaleite) by including the EPI contribution to the total energy. This is the most accurate ab initio total energy reported till date. The present work also opens the way to compute the ab initio free-energy more accurately at finite temperatures by including the EPI contribution.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a corrected non-adiabatic expression for the partial-Fan-Migdal-occupied term in the electron-phonon interaction Hamiltonian, showing it is a higher-order term rather than second-order, and presents the first computation of EPI contributions to total energy for Carbon polymorphs (diamond and lonsdaleite), achieving the most accurate ab initio total energy reported.
AI.motivation: To correct the standard Hamiltonian for coupled electron-phonon systems by revealing that the partial-FM-occupied term is actually a higher-order term (not second-order), and to compute EPI contributions to total energy more accurately, especially for IR-active and IR-inactive materials.
AI.method: The authors derive a new expression for the partial-FM-occ contribution within the non-adiabatic approximation, showing its higher-order structure, and perform ab initio computations of the full EPI contribution to total energy for diamond and hexagonal lonsdaleite.
AI.result: The partial-FM-occ term is a higher-order term, not second-order. The new expressions capture the complete physics. First-ever computation of EPI contribution to total energy for Carbon polymorphs was performed, yielding the most accurate ab initio total energy reported to date.
AI.conclusion: The new expressions for the partial-FM-occ term should replace standard expressions in theoretical and computational studies. EPI contribution to total energy must be computed in the non-adiabatic approximation for all materials. This work enables more accurate ab initio free-energy calculations at finite temperatures.

title: Probing the Chirality of Trigonal Selenium and Tellurium by Spin and Orbital Hall Effects
summary: Chiral crystals exhibit enantiomer-dependent transport phenomena that generate pure spin or orbital currents, while the handedness sensitivity of spin and orbital Hall conductivities (SHC/OHC) remains insufficiently understood. Using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that trigonal selenium and tellurium -- prototypical chiral semiconductors -- exhibit opposite signs of the SHC/OHC tensor elements $σ_{yx}^{S_y}$ and $σ_{yx}^{L_y}$ between their left- and right-handed enantiomers. This behavior originates from the mirror operation relating the two structures, described by space groups $P3_221$ (left-handed) and $P3_121$ (right-handed). Although both enantiomers share identical band structures and four nonzero SHC/OHC tensor components, $σ_{yx}^{S_y}$ and $σ_{yx}^{L_y}$ reverse sign due to the antisymmetric transformation of the spin/orbital Berry curvature under the $M_{xy}$ mirror operation. More generally, for mirror-related enantiomorphic structures, selected SHC/OHC tensor components can exhibit symmetry-governed sign reversal. For trigonal Se and Te, the calculated signs of these components can be directly correlated with the left- and right-handed structures under the chosen coordinate convention. These results clarify the symmetry origin of handedness-dependent SHC/OHC and suggest a possible route for correlating measurable SHC/OHC signals with structural handedness in specific chiral materials.

AI.tldr: First-principles calculations reveal that trigonal selenium and tellurium exhibit opposite signs of spin and orbital Hall conductivities between left- and right-handed enantiomers, originating from mirror-operation-induced sign reversal of Berry curvature.
AI.motivation: To understand why chiral crystals exhibit handedness-dependent spin and orbital Hall conductivities, which remains insufficiently understood despite known enantiomer-dependent transport phenomena.
AI.method: First-principles calculations of spin Hall conductivity (SHC) and orbital Hall conductivity (OHC) in trigonal selenium and tellurium, analyzing left-handed (P3₂21) and right-handed (P3₁21) enantiomers.
AI.result: Both enantiomers share identical band structures and four nonzero SHC/OHC tensor components, but σ_{yx}^{S_y} and σ_{yx}^{L_y} reverse sign due to antisymmetric transformation of spin/orbital Berry curvature under M_{xy} mirror operation.
AI.conclusion: The symmetry origin of handedness-dependent SHC/OHC is clarified, and measurable SHC/OHC signals can be correlated with structural handedness in specific chiral materials.

title: Methane hydrate nucleation frustration and dimensional reduction of structural order under nanoconfinement
summary: Methane hydrate nucleation under nanoconfinement remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay between geometric restriction and molecular ordering. Here, we investigate the structural organization of water-methane systems confined between silica planar slit pores with widths ranging from 1 to 5 nm and temperatures between 250 and 295 K. Three-dimensional radial distribution functions reveal a clear suppression of hydrate-like ordering at strong confinement (below 2 nm), indicating frustrated nucleation. In contrast, projected two-dimensional correlations exhibit pronounced in-plane structural organization, evidencing a confinement-induced reduction in the dimensionality of molecular order.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates methane hydrate nucleation in nanoconfined silica slit pores (1-5 nm width, 250-295 K), finding that strong confinement below 2 nm suppresses hydrate-like ordering while promoting in-plane structural organization, indicating a dimensionality reduction in molecular order.
AI.motivation: To understand how nanoconfinement affects methane hydrate nucleation, which is poorly understood due to the complex interplay between geometric restriction and molecular ordering.
AI.method: The authors studied water-methane systems confined between silica planar slit pores with widths of 1-5 nm at temperatures between 250-295 K, using three-dimensional radial distribution functions and projected two-dimensional correlations to analyze structural organization.
AI.result: 3D radial distribution functions show suppressed hydrate-like ordering under strong confinement (below 2 nm), indicating frustrated nucleation. Projected 2D correlations reveal pronounced in-plane structural organization, demonstrating confinement-induced reduction in dimensionality of molecular order.
AI.conclusion: Strong nanoconfinement (<2 nm) frustrates methane hydrate nucleation by suppressing 3D hydrate-like ordering while enhancing 2D in-plane organization, revealing a dimensionality reduction mechanism in confined systems.

title: Biquadratic exchange coupling effect on the magnetic properties of (Fe/Ti) multilayers
summary: This work explores the static and dynamic magnetic properties of weakly antiferromagnetically coupled Fe/Ti superlattices, emphasizing the link between magnetic behavior and structural characteristics. HRTEM and XRD analyses confirm alternating Fe and Ti layers with rough interfaces, especially in upper layers. Magnetic measurements reveal two-step hysteresis loops and a temperature and thickness-dependent interlayer exchange coupling (IEC). A macrospin model incorporating bilinear and biquadratic coupling reproduces the experimental data and supports a phase diagram analysis identifying non-collinear configurations. The results underscore the impact of structural imperfections and highlight the crucial role of biquadratic exchange in Fe/Ti/Fe multilayers.

AI.tldr: This study investigates static and dynamic magnetic properties of weakly antiferromagnetically coupled Fe/Ti superlattices, finding that structural imperfections (rough interfaces) lead to two-step hysteresis loops and temperature/thickness-dependent interlayer exchange coupling. A macrospin model with bilinear and biquadratic coupling reproduces experiments and reveals non-collinear magnetic configurations, emphasizing biquadratic exchange's crucial role.
AI.motivation: To explore the relationship between magnetic behavior and structural characteristics in Fe/Ti superlattices with weak antiferromagnetic coupling, particularly how interfacial roughness affects magnetic properties.
AI.method: HRTEM and XRD for structural characterization; magnetic measurements for static/dynamic properties; macrospin model incorporating bilinear and biquadratic coupling; phase diagram analysis for identifying non-collinear configurations.
AI.result: Two-step hysteresis loops observed; interlayer exchange coupling (IEC) is temperature- and thickness-dependent; macrospin model with biquadratic exchange successfully reproduces experimental data; non-collinear configurations identified via phase diagram analysis.
AI.conclusion: Structural imperfections significantly impact magnetic behavior; biquadratic exchange plays a crucial role in determining the magnetic configuration of Fe/Ti/Fe multilayers.

title: Tunable Dual-Type Weyl Points in Dirac-Weyl Semimetal CaAgBi
summary: Dirac-Weyl semimetals host both Dirac and Weyl fermions and the exploration of material candidates with tunable topological properties is essential to realize topological spintronic devices. In this work, we propose CaAgBi as a Dirac-Weyl semimetal with tunable type-I and type-II Weyl points based on first-principle calculations. In addition to the three pairs of Dirac points located along the rotational axis as previously reported, our calculations reveal 18 additional pairs of dual-type Weyl points distributed across three distinct planes: type-I in the $k_z=0$ plane and type-II in the $k_z= \pm 0.0698\,\frac{2π}{c}$ planes. The topological features are further confirmed through chirality of the Weyl points as well as the existence of surface Fermi arcs. Moreover, we find that the position and annihilation of Dirac and Weyl points are tunable by the alloy engineering and external strains. The alloy engineering is employed to modulate the positions of Weyl points, revealing different annihilation concentrations for type-I and type-II Weyl points, potentially offering novel experimental strategies for Weyl point manipulation. Under tensile biaxial strain, the Weyl points in the $k_{z}=0$ plane annihilate along the $Γ$--$\mathrm{M}$ path at $2.1\%$ strain, whereas the Weyl points in the $k_{z}\neq 0$ planes remain robust within $6\%$ strain. This work provides a versatile platform for manipulating Dirac/Weyl interactions, with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) driven alloy control and strain-selective engineering opening avenues for topological electronics.

AI.tldr: CaAgBi is identified as a Dirac-Weyl semimetal with 18 additional dual-type Weyl points (type-I in $k_z=0$, type-II in $k_z=\pm0.0698\,2\pi/c$) beyond three known Dirac pairs. Topological features (chirality, Fermi arcs) are confirmed, and both alloy engineering and external biaxial strain can tune, annihilate, or selectively preserve these Weyl points, offering a platform for topological electronics.
AI.motivation: To discover material candidates that host both Dirac and Weyl fermions with tunable topological properties for topological spintronic device applications.
AI.method: First-principle calculations (density functional theory) to compute band structure, Weyl point chirality, surface Fermi arcs; alloy engineering to modulate Weyl point positions and annihilation concentrations; application of external biaxial strain to selectively annihilate Weyl points.
AI.result:
- 18 additional dual-type Weyl points found (type-I in $k_z=0$, type-II in $k_z=\pm0.0698\,2\pi/c$).
- Chirality and surface Fermi arcs confirm topological nature.
- Alloy engineering yields different annihilation concentrations for type-I vs. type-II Weyl points.
- Biaxial strain at 2.1% annihilates $k_z=0$ Weyl points along Γ-M; $k_z
eq0$ Weyl points remain robust up to 6% strain.
AI.conclusion: CaAgBi is a versatile platform for manipulating Dirac/Weyl interactions via SOC-driven alloy control and strain-selective engineering, opening new pathways for topological electronics.

title: N-Graphdiyne as a Tunable Platform for Stabilizing Light Metals toward High-Capacity Reversible Hydrogen Storage
summary: Hydrogen (H2) is a promising carbon-neutral energy carrier. However, its deployment is limited by the lack of lightweight, reversible storage media that operate under practical conditions. Here, we establish nitrogen-doped graphdiyne (N-GDY) as a programmable two-dimensional platform for stabilizing dispersed light-metal dopants and enabling high-capacity physisorption of molecular H2. The computational package involves density functional theory (DFT) combined with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and Langmuir-based statistical thermodynamic modeling. The results revealed that N-sites of N-GDY bind up to five Li, Na, K, and Ca atoms per primitive cell with binding energies of -2.27, -1.57, -1.80, and -2.13 eV, respectively, exceeding their respective bulk cohesive energies. AIMD simulations at 400 K further confirm the structural robustness of the decorated frameworks and the absence of metal aggregation. The polarised metal centres activate reversible H2 adsorption through electrostatic and dispersion interactions, with average adsorption energies falling within the optimal window (-0.15 to -0.35 eV per H2). Sequential adsorption analysis reveals uptake of up to 25 H2 molecules per primitive cell, achieving intrinsic gravimetric capacities of 13.08, 10.82, 9.23, and 9.15 wt% for Li-, Na-, K-, and Ca-functionalized systems, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis indicates favorable adsorption-desorption behavior under near-ambient conditions, with Li- and Ca-functionalized systems exceeding the 6.5 wt% U.S. Department of Energy's ultimate system-level target when considering intrinsic material capacity. These results identify N-GDY as a chemically tunable scaffold for dispersing lightweight metals and provide a mechanistic design strategy for achieving high-capacity, reversible hydrogen storage in porous two-dimensional materials.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes nitrogen-doped graphdiyne (N-GDY) as a programmable 2D platform for stabilizing dispersed light-metal dopants (Li, Na, K, Ca) that enable high-capacity reversible hydrogen physisorption. DFT, AIMD, and thermodynamic modeling show up to 13.08 wt% gravimetric H2 capacity with Li-functionalized N-GDY, exceeding the DOE's 6.5 wt% system-level target.
AI.motivation: Hydrogen is a promising carbon-neutral energy carrier but its deployment is limited by the lack of lightweight, reversible storage media that operate under practical conditions. The authors aim to address this gap by designing a 2D platform for hydrogen storage.
AI.method: The computational study employs density functional theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations at 400 K, and Langmuir-based statistical thermodynamic modeling to investigate N-GDY decorated with Li, Na, K, and Ca.
AI.result: N-sites of N-GDY bind up to five Li, Na, K, and Ca atoms per primitive cell with binding energies of -2.27, -1.57, -1.80, and -2.13 eV respectively. Sequential adsorption achieves up to 25 H2 molecules per primitive cell, with gravimetric capacities of 13.08, 10.82, 9.23, and 9.15 wt% for Li-, Na-, K-, and Ca-functionalized systems. Li- and Ca-functionalized systems exceed the DOE's 6.5 wt% ultimate system-level target.
AI.conclusion: N-GDY is identified as a chemically tunable scaffold for dispersing lightweight metals, providing a mechanistic design strategy for achieving high-capacity, reversible hydrogen storage in porous two-dimensional materials.

title: Agentic Design of Compositional Descriptors via Autoresearch for Materials Science Applications
summary: Autoresearch offers a flexible paradigm for automating scientific tasks, in which an AI agent proposes, implements, evaluates, and refines candidate solutions against a quantitative objective. Here, we use composition-based materials-property prediction to test whether such agents can perform a task beyond model selection and hyperparameter optimization: the design of input descriptors. We introduce Automat, an autoresearch framework where a coding agent based on a large language model generates composition-only descriptors for chemical compounds and evaluates them using a random forest workflow. The agent is restricted to information derivable from chemical formulas and iteratively proposes, implements, and tests chemically motivated descriptor strategies. We apply Automat, with OpenAI Codex using GPT-5.5 as the coding agent, to the prediction of experimental band gaps in inorganic materials and Curie temperatures in ferromagnetic compounds. In both tasks, Automat improves over fractional-composition, Magpie, and combined fractional-composition/Magpie baselines, while producing descriptor families that are chemically interpretable. These results provide a demonstration that autoresearch agents can generate competitive, task-specific materials descriptors without manual feature engineering during the run. They also reveal current limitations, including descriptor redundancy, sensitivity to greedy feature expansion, and the need for explicit complexity control, descriptor pruning, and more sophisticated search strategies.

AI.tldr: Automat, an autoresearch framework using GPT-5.5-based coding agents, generates composition-only descriptors for materials property prediction, outperforming fractional-composition, Magpie, and combined baselines on band gap and Curie temperature prediction tasks while producing chemically interpretable descriptor families.
AI.motivation: To test whether AI autoresearch agents can perform a task beyond model selection and hyperparameter optimization—specifically, the design of input descriptors for materials science.
AI.method: Automat framework: a GPT-5.5 (Codex) coding agent iteratively proposes, implements, and evaluates chemically motivated descriptor strategies derived solely from chemical formulas, using a random forest workflow for prediction tasks.
AI.result: Automat improved over fractional-composition, Magpie, and combined fractional-composition/Magpie baselines for both experimental band gap prediction (inorganic materials) and Curie temperature prediction (ferromagnetic compounds), producing chemically interpretable descriptor families.
AI.conclusion: Autoresearch agents can generate competitive, task-specific materials descriptors without manual feature engineering, though limitations remain including descriptor redundancy, sensitivity to greedy feature expansion, need for complexity control, descriptor pruning, and more sophisticated search strategies.

title: Telecom-Wavelength-Compatible Quantum Information Transcription Using Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers
summary: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a leading platform for solid-state quantum sensing and quantum information processing. While most optical studies rely on the visible fluorescence associated with the triplet transitions, the infrared singlet transition near $1042$ nm, which is typically considered dark within the singlet manifold of the NV optical cycle, provides an alternative optical channel. Here, we report wavelength-resolved optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) measurements of this infrared emission. We directly observe ODMR contrast in the $1042$ nm emission and analyze its dependence on the magnetic field. The field-dependent spectral dispersion of the ODMR signal demonstrates that the spin-state information encoded in the NV center is transcribed to the infrared singlet emission through the spin-selective intersystem crossing, in close analogy to the visible fluorescence readout. These results establish infrared ODMR as a high-fidelity optical readout pathway. Crucially, by extending spin-state transcription directly into the $1300-1600$ nm range, this work demonstrates a direct, conversion-free interface between diamond spin-qubits and standard telecommunication infrastructure, bypassing the efficiency bottlenecks of active frequency conversion and benefiting from the already well-developed technologies in this range of the electromagnetic spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates wavelength-resolved ODMR measurements of the 1042 nm infrared singlet emission from NV centers in diamond, showing spin-state information is transcribed to this emission via spin-selective intersystem crossing, and extends this readout to the 1300-1600 nm telecom range for direct integration with fiber-optic infrastructure.
AI.motivation: To establish an alternative optical readout pathway for NV centers via the infrared singlet transition near 1042 nm, and to extend spin-state readout directly into telecommunication wavelength bands (1300-1600 nm) to bypass efficiency bottlenecks of active frequency conversion.
AI.method: Wavelength-resolved optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) measurements of the 1042 nm infrared emission from NV centers, analyzing ODMR contrast as a function of magnetic field and spectral dispersion.
AI.result: Direct observation of ODMR contrast in the 1042 nm emission; field-dependent spectral dispersion showing spin-state information is transcribed via spin-selective intersystem crossing, analogous to visible fluorescence readout. Extension of spin-state transcription into the 1300-1600 nm telecom range.
AI.conclusion: Infrared ODMR provides a high-fidelity optical readout pathway for NV centers and enables a direct, conversion-free interface between diamond spin-qubits and standard telecommunication infrastructure.

title: Thermal expansion of FeWO$_4$ (Ferberite) and FeWO$_4$:Fe$_2$WO$_6$ (7:1): a comparative X-ray and neutron diffraction study
summary: The thermal expansion of natural FeWO$_4$ (ferberite) and synthetic FeWO$_4$:Fe$_2$WO$_6$ (7:1) was investigated over the 2-1123 K temperature range combining single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction together with neutron powder diffraction. High-precision lattice parameters were obtained for both samples. The temperature dependence of the unit-cell volume was analysed using physically based thermodynamic models, including the Kroll and Berman approaches as implemented in EoSFit7. All datasets are well reproduced within their respective temperature intervals. However, significant differences are observed between the behavior of ferberite and FeWO$_4$:Fe$_2$WO$_6$, which has a \~40% smaller thermal expansion coefficient and a reduced reference volume. Possible origins, including microstructural and phase-coexistence effects, are discussed. The results provide a comprehensive description of the thermal expansion behavior of FeWO$_4$ across a wide temperature range.

AI.tldr: The thermal expansion of natural FeWO₄ (ferberite) and synthetic FeWO₄:Fe₂WO₆ (7:1) was studied from 2–1123 K using single-crystal, powder X-ray, and neutron powder diffraction. The synthetic sample shows ~40% smaller thermal expansion and reduced reference volume; possible microstructural and phase-coexistence origins are discussed.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive, high-precision characterization of the thermal expansion behavior of FeWO₄ (ferberite) across a very wide temperature range (2–1123 K), and to understand differences between natural and synthetic samples.
AI.method: Combined single-crystal X-ray diffraction, powder X-ray diffraction, and neutron powder diffraction over 2–1123 K; thermodynamic modeling using Kroll and Berman approaches in EoSFit7.
AI.result: High-precision lattice parameters obtained; synthetic FeWO₄:Fe₂WO₆ exhibits ~40% smaller thermal expansion coefficient and reduced reference volume compared to natural ferberite.
AI.conclusion: The thermal expansion of FeWO₄ is comprehensively described; differences between natural and synthetic samples likely arise from microstructural effects and phase coexistence.

title: Melting Behavior and Phase Stability of CaO from Neural Network Potentials: a Molecular Dynamics Study
summary: We investigate the melting behavior of calcium oxide (CaO) under extreme conditions, a problem that remains poorly constrained due to experimental limitations despite its relevance for geophysical and technological applications. We develop a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP) for CaO with PANNA 2.0 and the LATTE descriptor, training it on a dataset of $\sim$12,000 configurations including solid, liquid, interfacial, and void-containing structures, extracted from ab-initio molecular dynamics data employing PBEsol exchange-correlation functional. We perform large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to compute the melting temperature at ambient pressure using both the void-nucleated melting (VNM) and two-phase coexistence (TPC) methods, obtaining $T_m=3055\pm11$ K and $T_m=2847\pm15$ K, respectively.\\ We calculate an enthalpy of fusion of $ΔH_f\sim73$ kJ/mol, in agreement with thermodynamic assessments and ab initio calculations. We also reproduce the thermal expansion and obtain a volume increase of $\sim$29% at Tm, consistent with the corresponding decrease in density extracted from spatially resolved number density profiles. Finally, we calculate the high-pressure melting curve of CaO up to 20 GPa, providing one of the very few computational determinations of this quantity to date. The results confirm that the overheating ratio $η$ is not constant under pressure, increasing from 17% at ambient pressure to 24% at 20 GPa, confirming previous findings and ruling out the assumption of a fixed overheating ratio. Our results establish MLIP-based simulations as a robust and efficient framework for investigating phase stability in ionic oxides and provide new insight into the melting behavior of CaO under extreme conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) for CaO to investigate its melting behavior under extreme conditions, reporting melting temperatures at ambient pressure via two methods, enthalpy of fusion, thermal expansion, and the high-pressure melting curve up to 20 GPa, demonstrating that the overheating ratio is not constant under pressure.
AI.motivation: The melting behavior of CaO under extreme conditions remains poorly constrained due to experimental limitations, despite its importance for geophysical (e.g., planetary interiors) and technological applications.
AI.method: A Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP) for CaO was developed using PANNA 2.0 and the LATTE descriptor, trained on ~12,000 configurations (solid, liquid, interfacial, void-containing) from ab-initio molecular dynamics with the PBEsol functional. Melting temperatures were computed via void-nucleated melting (VNM) and two-phase coexistence (TPC) methods in large-scale MD simulations.
AI.result: Melting temperatures at ambient pressure: $T_m=3055\pm11$ K (VNM) and $T_m=2847\pm15$ K (TPC). Enthalpy of fusion $\Delta H_f\sim73$ kJ/mol, volume increase ~29% at $T_m$. High-pressure melting curve computed up to 20 GPa. Overheating ratio increases from 17% at ambient pressure to 24% at 20 GPa.
AI.conclusion: MLIP-based simulations provide a robust framework for studying phase stability in ionic oxides. The overheating ratio is not constant under pressure, ruling out the assumption of a fixed overheating ratio. The study offers new computational insights into CaO melting under extreme conditions.

title: Generative reconstruction of 2D and 3D polycrystalline microstructures using symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics
summary:
Establishing structure-property linkages in polycrystalline materials requires representative two- (2D) and three- (3D) dimensional microstructural inputs for full-field simulations. A core objective of microstructure characterization and reconstruction is the generative synthesis of 2D and 3D microstructures that reflect a target statistical ensemble using limited 2D data as a reference. This work introduces an orientation-based differentiable microstructure characterization and reconstruction framework, implemented in MCRpy, to perform reconstructions of voxelized images. Unit quaternions in combination with symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics are utilized to derive a continuous, symmetry-invariant representation of crystallographic orientations to overcome the numerical singularities and discontinuities associated with traditional Euler-based methods.
  The descriptor-based reconstructions are driven by a set combining two-point spatial correlations, a novel hybrid three-point variogram, and a mean variation regularizer to capture both global texture and local interfacial topology. The framework's efficiency is demonstrated by reconstructing 3D realizations from 2D orientation data of an aluminum alloy after thermo-mechanical processing, successfully recovering both morphological features and crystallographic distribution. Systematic benchmarking indicates that second-order gradient-based optimization, utilizing the L-BFGS-B algorithm, effectively navigates the complex loss landscape to generate high-fidelity realizations with minimal residuals. This methodology provides a versatile, open-source framework for the digital synthesis of polycrystalline representative volume elements to facilitate the rapid development of microstructure-informed materials design workflows.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an orientation-based differentiable microstructure characterization and reconstruction framework (MCRpy) that uses unit quaternions and symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics to reconstruct 3D polycrystalline microstructures from limited 2D orientation data, employing two-point spatial correlations, a hybrid three-point variogram, and a mean variation regularizer with L-BFGS-B optimization.
AI.motivation: To establish structure-property linkages in polycrystalline materials, representative 2D and 3D microstructural inputs are needed for full-field simulations. Current methods face numerical singularities and discontinuities with traditional Euler-based orientation representations, motivating a more robust differentiable framework for microstructure characterization and reconstruction from limited 2D data.
AI.method: The framework uses unit quaternions combined with symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics for continuous, symmetry-invariant orientation representation. Reconstruction is driven by a combined descriptor set of two-point spatial correlations, a novel hybrid three-point variogram, and a mean variation regularizer. Second-order gradient-based optimization with L-BFGS-B algorithm navigates the loss landscape for high-fidelity reconstruction.
AI.result: Successfully reconstructed 3D realizations from 2D orientation data of a thermo-mechanically processed aluminum alloy, recovering both morphological features and crystallographic distribution. Benchmarking shows L-BFGS-B optimization effectively generates high-fidelity realizations with minimal residuals.
AI.conclusion: The methodology provides a versatile, open-source framework for digital synthesis of polycrystalline representative volume elements, facilitating rapid development of microstructure-informed materials design workflows.

title: The Emergence of Photonic Crystalline Order and Time-Series Dynamics in NaCl Droplet Deposition
summary: Crystallization during droplet evaporation gives rise to complex, self-organized structures, yet the mechanisms underlying the emergence of ordered functional phases remain poorly understood. In this study, we present a comprehensive, multi-scale investigation into the crystallization dynamics of NaCl during droplet evaporation on a germanium (001) substrate, relevant for its IR applications. Through systematic microscopic characterization, we identify the formation of diverse microstructures, including 1D photonic crystal nanostructures formed within hybrid crystal-glass photonic system. To enable quantitative comparison across experimental conditions, we introduce the NaCl equivalent height as a unified metric to describe and classify the evolution of crystalline morphology. Our results reveal that diffusion anisotropy, rather than growth kinetics, primarily governs the maximal attainable structure size. Quantitative thin film interference analysis demonstrates the presence of discrete thickness layers in the film. Controlled evaporation experiments yield homogeneous crystallization patterns across the entire droplet area, facilitating the emergence of ordered photonic structures. Time-series dynamics analysis of height profiles uncovered the spatiotemporal evolution of the crystallization front, providing insights into the details of underlying physical mechanisms. Together, these results establish a robust experimental framework for understanding and predicting crystallization behavior in evaporating droplets, with potential applications in materials synthesis, photonics, and microscale pattern formation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates NaCl crystallization dynamics during droplet evaporation on a germanium substrate, revealing that diffusion anisotropy governs structure size and that controlled evaporation enables ordered photonic crystal formation. A unified metric (NaCl equivalent height) is introduced to classify crystalline morphology evolution.
AI.motivation: The mechanisms underlying the emergence of ordered functional phases during crystallization in evaporating droplets remain poorly understood, despite the importance of these self-organized structures.
AI.method: Multi-scale investigation combining systematic microscopic characterization, thin film interference analysis, time-series dynamics of height profiles, and controlled evaporation experiments on a germanium (001) substrate. Introduced NaCl equivalent height as a unified metric for quantitative comparison.
AI.result: Diffusion anisotropy primarily governs maximal attainable structure size, not growth kinetics. Discrete thickness layers exist in the film. Controlled evaporation yields homogeneous crystallization and ordered photonic structures across the droplet area.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a robust experimental framework for understanding and predicting crystallization behavior in evaporating droplets, with potential applications in materials synthesis, photonics, and microscale pattern formation.

title: Limitations of Debye-Waller lattice temperature extraction under electronic excitation
summary: Ultrafast diffraction is the cutting-edge technique to extract the atomic temperature at femtosecond timescales, and further related quantities - in particular, electron-phonon coupling strength at elevated electronic temperatures. The present work demonstrates limitations of such an analysis, emphasizing the importance of careful evaluation of the evolution of the Debye temperature. It is shown that, due to the sensitivity of the Debye-Waller analysis to this parameter, neglecting its changes under electronic excitation may lead to significant deviations of the atomic temperature extracted from its true values.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that neglecting changes in the Debye temperature under electronic excitation can cause significant errors in atomic temperature extraction from ultrafast diffraction experiments, impacting measurements of electron-phonon coupling strength.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate limitations in ultrafast diffraction analysis for extracting atomic temperature and electron-phonon coupling strength, specifically highlighting the critical role of Debye temperature evolution under electronic excitation.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis examining the sensitivity of Debye-Waller analysis to changes in the Debye temperature under electronic excitation conditions.
AI.result: Neglecting Debye temperature changes leads to significant deviations between extracted and true atomic temperatures during ultrafast diffraction measurements.
AI.conclusion: Careful evaluation of Debye temperature evolution is essential for accurate ultrafast diffraction analysis of atomic temperature and electron-phonon coupling.
